title: Four ways to initialise a variable

prereqs.why: The whole program is the four forms side by side, and the output is what each one produces.

statement:
C++ gives a variable its first value in several different ways, and they do not all mean the same thing.

**What does this print?** Four lines.
hints: Three of these four give the variable the number written next to it. Work those out first and the only question left is the fourth.
`int e{};` has nothing between the braces. That form has a name — value initialisation — and it does something specific rather than nothing.
An `int` with empty braces is zero. Not undefined, not arbitrary: zero, guaranteed.
